title: Cap. IX Arg. 10 Sol cont.: Scripture — Gospel an odor of death from hearers' voluntary rebellion, not from God's primary intention (2 Cor. ii; Heb. ii; Acts xiii; Col. i)
pass_a_gloss: For the Scriptures themselves determine far otherwise of Evangelical preaching; namely that unto some it becomes an odor of death unto death, 2 Cor. ii. 15, 16. yet not from the primary intention of God, but from their voluntary rebellion, Hebr. ii. 3. How shall we escape, if we neglect so great salvation? Actor. xiii. 38. Remission of sins through Christ is announced unto you, etc. and 46. After ye put it from you, and judge yourselves unworthy of everlasting life. And Coloss. i. 28. We announce Christ, admonishing every man, and teaching every man, that we may present every man perfect in Christ Jesus.
pass_b_english: Scripture itself settles Gospel preaching far differently: to some it becomes an odor of death unto death (2 Cor. ii. 15–16) — not from God's primary intention, but from their voluntary rebellion (Heb. ii. 3: How shall we escape if we neglect so great a salvation?). Acts xiii. 38: Remission of sins through Christ is announced to you — and 46: After you put it from you and judge yourselves unworthy of everlasting life. Col. i. 28: We announce Christ, admonishing and teaching every one, that we may present every one perfect in Christ Jesus.
source_text: Ipsae enim Scripturae de Evangelica praedicatione longe aliter statuunt; fieri nimirum quibusdam odorem mortis ad mortem, 2 Cor. ii. 15, 16. sed non ex primaria Dei intentione, verum ex voluntaria illorum rebellione, Hebr. ii. 3. Quomodo nos effugiemus, si tantam neglexerimus salutem? Actor. xiii. 38. Annunciatur vobis remissio peccatorum per Christum, etc. et 46. Postquam repellitis illam, et indignos vos decernitis vita aeterna. Et Coloss. i. 28. Annunciamus Christum, admonentes quosvis, et quosvis erudientes, ut quosvis sistamus perfectos in Christo Jesu.
